Plain serde data only: no handles, no connections, so an adapter can
later run out of process behind a pipe. The descriptor is self-describing —
entity kinds, auth methods and write ops drive the UI, so nothing

changing anything here breaks every adapter at once.

div.p:
knobas-db and knobas-search depend on no knobas crate at all.
knobas-sync does not depend on knobas-db: the engine takes a PgPool
it is handed and never opens one, so it is usable from the app, from a
scheduler and from a test. knobas-db is its dev-dependency only.

p.strong: ① knobas provisions and ADOPTS its own PostgreSQL.

div.p:
Nothing is installed or configured by hand. There is no brew install postgresql.
EmbeddedDb::start downloads PG 18.6 once per machine into ~/.theseus (shared binaries),
initdbs a data directory under the app data dir, and serves it on loopback TCP —
never a unix socket, whose path under Application Support would exceed macOS' 103 bytes.
If a server is already serving that data directory — a knobas killed by Ctrl-C never
runs its shutdown — it is adopted, not refused and not killed: the orphan becomes
this run's warm start. An adopted handle owns nothing, so no later quit ever stops it.
A stale postmaster.pid is cleared only when both the port is dead and the pid is gone.
KNOBAS_DB_URL points the app at a server somebody else manages instead.

p.strong: ② sync.item is a MIRROR; knobas.* is OWNED data.

div.p:
Every synced item writes two rows, and they answer different questions.
knobas.entity is the durable identity: links, notes and activity all reference it.
sync.item is the refreshable mirror — title, body, author, and the raw source payload,
kept so items can be re-mapped later without re-fetching. Rewritten wholesale every run.
A remote deletion therefore only sets knobas.entity.deleted_at. The mirror row stays, so
the UI can still show the last-known title of something that vanished upstream.
"Deleted" lives on the entity alone ⇒ every reader of the mirror must join knobas.entity.
The in-flight migration makes that structural: the view sync.live_item.
A full sync does not yet reconcile hard deletes; the sweep is still to come.

p.strong: ③ The mock adapter is a certified Source, not a test double.

div.p:
knobas-source-mock passes the identical contract::battery every real adapter must pass:
declared kinds only · the same fault classes from test_connection and from sync ·
undeclared write ops refused · sink failures propagated, never swallowed ·
an idle sync returning the cursor it was given, unchanged.
So the whole app can be built, demoed and tested end to end before Jira, Gitea or
TeamCity exist — and a new adapter has a correct worked example to copy.

p.strong: ④ One gate, run identically by a developer and by CI.

div.p:
just check = cargo fmt · svelte-check + vite build · clippy --all-targets ·
clippy --lib (the features a consumer actually gets) · cargo test over a real
embedded PostgreSQL that the test harness starts once per test binary.
.github/workflows/check.yml does nothing but put a Linux machine in front of that
one command, so the gate and the developer can never disagree.
The in-flight branch adds tests/ipc.rs, which drives real commands through
tauri::test's mock runtime rather than trusting the documentation.
